key_insight: WEST is a scalable open-source excited-state simulation platform that combines GW, Bethe-Salpeter, TDDFT, and embedding methods in a common framework without explicit virtual states.
engineering_relevance: The code enables predictive modeling of optoelectronic and defect-driven processes in large materials systems, which is useful for designing next-generation solar-cell and photonic materials.
method: Full-frequency GW, BSE, and TDDFT in a unified plane-wave pseudopotential code
Avoids explicit virtual-state construction using DFPT/DMPT, low-rank screening, and localization
Hierarchical parallelization plus GPU acceleration for thousands of GPUs
evidence_signal: The abstract reports representative applications and near-ideal strong scaling to thousands of GPUs, including simulations of systems with more than a thousand atoms.
watch_item: Performance and accuracy depend on complex workflows and high-end GPU infrastructure, which may limit ease of adoption and reproducibility for smaller teams.
paper_title: The WEST code for large-scale excited-state materials simulations
